Additive relationship matrix from a pedigree

Source: R/makeA.R
makeA.Rd

Computes the numerator (additive) relationship matrix A from a pedigree, for use as the A argument of lmm_animal.

Usage

makeA(pedigree, Gamma = NULL, groups = NULL)

Arguments

pedigree

Data frame whose first three columns are the individual, its sire and its dam, with 0, NA or "" for unknown parents. Individuals can be in any order, and the pedigree can contain ancestors that have no records.

Gamma

Optional relationship matrix among the founders, or among founder groups when groups is given. Founders are the individuals with both parents unknown, including parents that were added because they were missing from the pedigree. The default NULL leaves founders unrelated, as in a standard pedigree. With groups = NULL, Gamma must have one row and column per founder, or founder IDs as row and column names; with groups, it must have one row and column per group, or the group labels as row and column names.

groups

Optional vector assigning each founder to a row and column of Gamma, for a metafounder or genetic-group model. It can be named with founder IDs, or unnamed with one entry per founder in pedigree order (individuals with both parents unknown, then any parents added as founders). When Gamma has no dimnames, groups are used in sort(unique(groups)) order.

Value

A symmetric positive-definite matrix with the individuals' IDs on both dimensions, in the order of pedigree.

Details

The additive relationship is computed with the tabular method: with \(s_i\) and \(d_i\) the parents of individual \(i\), $$A_{ii} = 1 + A_{s_i d_i} / 2, \qquad A_{ij} = (A_{s_i j} + A_{d_i j}) / 2,$$ taking a term as zero when the parent is unknown. The first line includes the inbreeding coefficient of \(i\) through the relationship between its parents, so pedigrees with inbreeding are handled. Individuals are processed in an order where parents come before their offspring, whatever order the pedigree is in, and a pedigree where an individual is its own ancestor is an error.

A parent that is not one of the individuals of the pedigree is added to A as a founder, with a warning, so a truncated pedigree or a mistyped ID does not silently drop the relationship. Subset A by name to match the rows of Y, or let animal_design do it.

animal_design calls this function when it is given pedigree and no genotypes.

With Gamma, the founder block of A is initialized with the founder relationships instead of the identity, and the same recursion propagates them. This is the \(A^\Gamma\) construction for related founders and metafounders (Legarra et al. 2015): \(\Gamma_{ii}\) is the relationship of founder \(i\) with itself and \(\Gamma_{ij}\) its relationship with founder \(j\), so a founder no longer has to have \(A_{ii} = 1\). When groups is given, founders in the same group share the diagonal of Gamma and different groups use its off-diagonals. A genomic relationship matrix among the founders, for example from genomic_relationship, can be used as Gamma, but it estimates realized relationships and is not the same as the base-population \(\Gamma\); shrinkage, such as the blend argument of genomic_relationship, is advisable.

Only founders with both parents unknown are given founder relationships. An unknown parent of an individual that has one known parent is still treated as an unrelated founder, as in the standard tabular method; to model those unknown parents as part of the related base population, add them explicitly to the pedigree and assign them to a group.

References

Legarra, A., Christensen, O. F., Vitezica, Z. G., Aguilar, I., & Misztal, I. (2015). Ancestral relationships using metafounders: finite ancestral populations and across population relationships. Genetics, 200(2), 455-468. doi:10.1534/genetics.115.177014

See also

genomic_relationship, animal_design

Examples

ped <- data.frame(id = 1:6, sire = c(0, 0, 1, 1, 4, 4),
                  dam = c(0, 0, 2, 2, 3, 5))
A <- makeA(ped)
round(A, 3)
#>     1   2     3     4    5     6
#> 1 1.0 0.0 0.500 0.500 0.50 0.500
#> 2 0.0 1.0 0.500 0.500 0.50 0.500
#> 3 0.5 0.5 1.000 0.500 0.75 0.625
#> 4 0.5 0.5 0.500 1.000 0.75 0.875
#> 5 0.5 0.5 0.750 0.750 1.25 1.000
#> 6 0.5 0.5 0.625 0.875 1.00 1.375
# full-sib mating: individual 6 is the offspring of the sibs 4 and 5
ped2 <- data.frame(id = 1:6, sire = c(NA, NA, NA, 1, 1, 4),
                   dam = c(NA, NA, NA, 2, 2, 5))
diag(makeA(ped2))   # 1.25 for the inbred individual
#>    1    2    3    4    5    6 
#> 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.25 

# related founders: founders 1 and 2 have relationship 0.5
Gamma <- matrix(c(1, 0.5, 0.5, 1), 2,
                dimnames = list(c("1", "2"), c("1", "2")))
ped3 <- data.frame(id = 1:4, sire = c(NA, NA, 1, 1),
                   dam = c(NA, NA, 2, 2))
A3 <- makeA(ped3, Gamma = Gamma)
round(A3, 3)
#>      1    2    3    4
#> 1 1.00 0.50 0.75 0.75
#> 2 0.50 1.00 0.75 0.75
#> 3 0.75 0.75 1.25 0.75
#> 4 0.75 0.75 0.75 1.25

# founder groups: 1 and 2 in group A, 3 in group B
Gamma_groups <- matrix(c(1, 0.2, 0.2, 1), 2,
                       dimnames = list(c("A", "B"), c("A", "B")))
ped4 <- data.frame(id = 1:5, sire = c(NA, NA, NA, 1, 1),
                   dam = c(NA, NA, NA, 2, 3))
round(makeA(ped4, Gamma = Gamma_groups, groups = c("A", "A", "B")), 3)
#>     1   2   3   4   5
#> 1 1.0 1.0 0.2 1.0 0.6
#> 2 1.0 1.0 0.2 1.0 0.6
#> 3 0.2 0.2 1.0 0.2 0.6
#> 4 1.0 1.0 0.2 1.5 0.6
#> 5 0.6 0.6 0.6 0.6 1.1
